settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: acceptableName still requires the parameter name to match acceptedPattern (ACCEPTED_PARAM_NAMES, line 145/438) and pass isExcluded (lines 411-417).
setExcludeParams still compiles and applies user-configured excludeParams patterns (lines 503-509); struts-default.xml configures excludeParams such as ^action:.*,^method:.*.
ReflectionContextState.setDenyMethodExecution(contextMap, true) is set around parameter setting (line 237), blocking method invocation.
The method-level details of OGNL evaluation / DefaultMemberAccess were not fully traced, so runtime exploitability is unconfirmed.
candidates.description: In xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/interceptor/ParametersInterceptor.java the setExcludeParams method compiles the configured exclude patterns but the statement that would always add ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN is commented out (line 510 is a 'Patch:' comment, line 511 is the commented-out add). The CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN ("(.*\\.|^|.*|\\[('|\"))class(\\.|('|\")]|\\[).*") defined in ExcludedPatterns is what rejects parameter names referencing 'class' / [class] style OGNL. With it disabled, filtering falls back to the interceptor's own accepted pattern (ACCEPTED_PARAM_NAMES) and whatever excludeParams the application configures. This is a candidate for weakened parameter-name filtering on the request-to-value-stack path. Note the accepted pattern and configured excludeParams still apply, and I did not trace whether a reachable top-level OGNL sink actually exists in this revision.
missing_evidence: No proof that a request parameter name referencing 'class' actually reaches SecurityMemberAccess.isAccessible and succeeds without the CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN.
No configuration (e.g. updated struts-default.xml) proving the pattern is supplied elsewhere to compensate.
No runtime test demonstrating a differential effect of the commented-out line.
preconditions: A deployed interceptor stack uses com.opensymphony.xwork2.interceptor.ParametersInterceptor (the default params interceptor).
The application relies on the built-in class-access blacklist rather than configuring its own complete excludeParams set.
An action/property graph reachable via OGNL setValue that can be influenced by a 'class' style key exists.
candidates.title: ParametersInterceptor class-access blacklist pattern is commented out (disabled check)

counter_evidence: acceptedPattern still restricts names to letters, digits, dot, ']', '[', '_' and whitespace (line 170), somewhat limiting arbitrary OGNL syntax.
Injection only occurs when cookiesNameSet contains '*' or exactly the cookie name (lines 227-233), so a restrictive cookiesName configuration prevents it.
No explicit setDenyMethodExecution guard is visible in this interceptor, but downstream OGNL SecurityMemberAccess/DefaultMemberAccess handling was not fully traced.
candidates.description: In core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/interceptor/CookieInterceptor.java, isAcceptableName (lines 247-250) returns acceptedPattern.matcher(name).matches() while the stronger check against ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN is left only as a commented-out 'Patch:' line (line 248). acceptedPattern is compiled from ACCEPTED_PATTERN = "[a-zA-Z0-9\\.\\]\\[_'\\s]+" (lines 170/176), which permits dots, brackets, underscores and single quotes but does not specifically reject 'class' or OGNL bracket/quote constructs. Cookie names arrive from the request (line 218 getCookies, line 223 getName) and, when the name filter passes and cookiesName matches (lines 226-234), populateCookieValueIntoStack passes the cookie value to stack.setValue(cookieName, cookieValue) (lines 261-287, notably 274 and 285). This is a candidate for untrusted-data injection into the value stack through a weakened cookie-name validation gate. Exploitability depends on cookiesName configuration and on the OGNL member-access guards, which were not fully traced.
missing_evidence: No configuration sample showing cookiesName='*' with cookiesValue='*' in this repository's shipped stacks.
No trace confirming stack.setValue leads to SecurityMemberAccess with allowStaticMethodAccess enabled or otherwise permits a sensitive operation.
No runtime test showing the weakened pattern permits a name that the CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN would have rejected.
preconditions: An action stack references the 'cookie' interceptor (CookieInterceptor) and configures cookiesName to include the malicious cookie name or '*'.
cookiesValue is empty or '*', or its set contains the attacker-controlled cookie value, so the value is injected.
A value-stack/action property path reachable by the (accepted) cookie name that yields a security-relevant OGNL operation.
candidates.title: CookieInterceptor injects cookie values using a weakened name-acceptance pattern instead of the class-access blacklist
